chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: The Strand Theater success and the Cab Drivers "Nature Boy" arrangement
summary: Reviewers called the Strand engagement Cab's best-sounding band; McRae wrote a chant ending and small-band numbers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Do you think that that changed any of the character of Cab's band? They didn't sound it like it did, but I mean, were there any observers at the time the band sounded --
Yeah. When we can in the Strand Theater -- it's a write-up someplace I got in
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

one of my scrapbooks -- I could go find it.
The guy wrote up and said Cab had one of the best sounding bands that he ever had. That was the same band. Said he always had (inaudible).
But you know what was about the band?
I had wrote a thing for him called Nature Boy. I wrote him an arrangement on that.
And on the end of the arrangement -- you know Cab do that Jewish chant thing? I put a Jewish chant thing on in there. In the end where he did that thing.
And he did that record -- he did it with the Cab Drivers. I did a little small arrangement on it and I did it with the Cab Drivers on the Strand Theater.
And he tore the theater up with that little small band arrangement. It was like --
Cozy Cole rolled out another set of drume (inaudible) on the platform. Whatchamacallem had the vibes -- Tyree Glen on Vibes and trombone.
And whatchamacallem on trumpet -- Jonah Jones on trumpet.

WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Shad Collins played in that little small band, right?
And I was on tenor in the rhythm section, you know. The piano player (inaudible) was right there and roll it down front. And that's what they call the Cab Drivers.
And I never forget, I wrote the thing for Cab, 'Nature Boy.' And I put this Jewish chant thing on the end. He go in there and do his thing and it was a big thing. (singing notes)
And Cab sung the devil out of it. Look like it was made for him. Just like -- the song was made for Cab.

I never heard anybody do it any better than Cab. And I put that little Jewish thing in 'put that little Jewish chant thing there there (singing notes) (inaudible), on the end.' And he did that and he tore that theater up.
And (inaudible) say that was the best sounding band that Cab ever had. But the band was together.
